notice: RN bank batch 15: Neurological II and sensory: spinal cord, degenerative disorders, eye and ear. DRAFT - every question must be reviewed by an RN or nurse educator before candidates rely on it.

subtopics.name: Care of clients with sensory impairment

questions.stem: A client has a complete spinal cord injury at the C4 level. What is the nurse's priority?

rationale.correct: "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive." High cervical injuries threaten breathing first.

perOption.a: C3 to C5 supply the phrenic nerve to the diaphragm; injury at C4 can cause respiratory failure.
perOption.b: This is important but comes after breathing.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize breathing in a cervical spinal cord injury.

questions.stem: A client with a T4 spinal cord injury suddenly has a pounding headache, a blood pressure of 210/110 mm Hg, flushing above the injury and a heart rate of 50/min. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Sit the client upright with the legs lowered

rationale.correct: Autonomic dysreflexia (injury at T6 or above): sit up, loosen clothing, find and remove the trigger (usually a full bladder, then the bowel or skin), and give medication if needed.

perOption.a: Raising the head lowers blood pressure quickly while the cause is found.
perOption.b: This comes after positioning and removing the trigger if the BP stays high.
perOption.c: Lying flat raises blood pressure further.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Respond to autonomic dysreflexia.

questions.stem: After sitting a client with autonomic dysreflexia upright, what should the nurse check next?

options.text: The bladder for distention and the catheter for kinks

rationale.correct: Common triggers: bladder distention, fecal impaction, tight clothing and pressure injuries.

perOption.a: A full bladder is the most common trigger.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Identify triggers of autonomic dysreflexia.

questions.stem: A client with an acute cervical spinal cord injury has a blood pressure of 78/40 mm Hg and a heart rate of 48/min, with warm, dry skin. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Neurogenic shock: hypotension, bradycardia and warm skin from loss of sympathetic tone.

perOption.a: Loss of sympathetic tone causes hypotension, bradycardia and warm, dry skin.
perOption.b: Hypovolemia causes tachycardia and cool skin.
perOption.d: There are no signs of infection.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize neurogenic shock.

questions.stem: A client has a halo vest for a cervical spine fracture. Which item must be kept with the client at all times?

options.text: The wrench for removing the vest's front panel

rationale.correct: Keep the wrench taped to the halo vest; never use the frame to move the client.

perOption.a: In a cardiac arrest, the front panel must be removed quickly for CPR.
perOption.b: The halo already stabilizes the neck.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Ensure halo vest emergency equipment is available.

questions.stem: Which intervention should the nurse include in a bowel program for a client with a spinal cord injury?

options.text: Scheduled toileting at the same time each day, with digital stimulation or a suppository as prescribed
Toileting only when the client feels the urge

rationale.correct: Bowel programs use regular timing, fiber, fluids and stimulation to prevent impaction, which can also trigger autonomic dysreflexia.

perOption.a: A consistent schedule trains the bowel and prevents incontinence and impaction.
perOption.d: The client may not feel the urge.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Plan a bowel program after spinal cord injury.

questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis has increasing weakness, trouble swallowing and a weak cough. What is the priority assessment?

rationale.correct: In myasthenic crisis, monitor breathing closely; intubation may be needed.

perOption.a: Myasthenic crisis can cause respiratory failure.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize assessment in a myasthenic crisis.

questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis takes pyridostigmine. When should the client take it?

options.text: 30 to 60 minutes before meals, exactly on schedule

rationale.correct: Cholinesterase inhibitors must be taken on time; too much causes cholinergic crisis (excess secretions, cramps, weakness).

perOption.a: Peak effect at mealtime helps chewing and swallowing; late doses worsen weakness.
perOption.c: It is taken on a schedule.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach timing of pyridostigmine.

questions.stem: A client with Guillain-Barré syndrome has weakness that started in the feet and is moving upward. What is the priority?

rationale.correct: Guillain-Barré causes ascending paralysis; watch vital capacity and the ability to swallow.

perOption.a: Ascending paralysis can reach the respiratory muscles.
perOption.c: Pain matters, but breathing comes first.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize breathing in Guillain-Barré syndrome.

questions.stem: A client with multiple sclerosis says symptoms get worse after a hot shower. What should the nurse teach?

rationale.correct: Clients with MS should avoid heat, fatigue, stress and infection, which can worsen symptoms.

perOption.a: Heat slows nerve conduction in demyelinated nerves (the Uhthoff phenomenon).
perOption.d: Heat sensitivity is common in MS.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach clients with MS to avoid heat.

questions.stem: A client with Parkinson's disease takes carbidopa-levodopa. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.text: "Spread protein out through the day and avoid large high-protein meals near your doses."
"Stop the medication if your urine darkens."

rationale.correct: Carbidopa-levodopa: orthostatic hypotension, dyskinesias, dark urine and protein interaction.

perOption.a: Dietary protein competes with levodopa for absorption.
perOption.b: B6 reduces the effect of levodopa alone; it matters less with carbidopa, but it isn't recommended.
perOption.c: Dark urine or sweat is harmless.
perOption.d: Orthostatic hypotension is common; rise slowly.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach about carbidopa-levodopa.

questions.stem: Which findings are expected in a client with Parkinson's disease? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tremor that appears only when reaching for an object

rationale.correct: Parkinson's: tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and postural instability (TRAP).

perOption.a: Resting tremor is a cardinal sign.
perOption.e: This intention tremor suggests a cerebellar problem.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize the signs of Parkinson's disease.

questions.stem: Which instruction should the nurse give a client with Parkinson's disease to reduce the risk of falls?

options.text: "Consciously lift your feet and take larger steps, with your feet apart."
"Look down at your feet while walking."

rationale.correct: Parkinson's gait training: big steps, wide base, swinging the arms and rocking to start if frozen.

perOption.a: This counteracts shuffling and improves balance.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach fall prevention in Parkinson's disease.

questions.stem: Which statement about amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is accurate?

options.text: Cognition usually stays intact while the muscles weaken

rationale.correct: ALS: progressive motor weakness with intact cognition; plan early for breathing and nutrition needs.

perOption.a: ALS affects motor neurons; most clients stay mentally alert.
perOption.d: Respiratory failure is the usual cause of death.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Understand the course of ALS.

questions.stem: A client with trigeminal neuralgia has facial pain triggered by touch. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.text: "I'll chew on the unaffected side and use lukewarm food."
"I'll rub my face to ease the pain."
"I'll use ice packs on my face."

rationale.correct: Trigeminal neuralgia: avoid triggers (touch, cold, chewing on the affected side); carbamazepine is often prescribed.

perOption.a: This avoids triggering the pain.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach a client with trigeminal neuralgia.

questions.stem: A client with Bell's palsy can't close the right eye. Which intervention is most important?

options.text: Use artificial tears and an eye patch or tape the eyelid closed at night
Keep the room dark at all times

rationale.correct: Bell's palsy: protect the eye, use moist heat and facial exercises; steroids are often prescribed.

perOption.a: This protects the cornea from drying and injury.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Protect the eye in Bell's palsy.

questions.stem: Before giving sumatriptan for a migraine, which client history should the nurse report to the provider?

rationale.correct: Triptans are contraindicated with coronary artery disease, uncontrolled hypertension and recent ergot use.

perOption.a: Triptans cause vasoconstriction and are contraindicated in coronary artery disease.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Identify contraindications to triptans.

questions.stem: A client had cataract surgery today. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll wear my eye shield at night."
"I'll bend over to tie my shoes."
"I'll use my eye drops as prescribed."

rationale.correct: After cataract surgery: avoid bending, lifting and straining; wear the shield; report pain or vision loss.

perOption.a: The shield protects the eye.
perOption.b: Bending raises eye pressure; the client should avoid bending and heavy lifting.
perOption.c: Sudden pain may signal a complication.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach a client after cataract surgery.

questions.stem: A client reports sudden severe eye pain, blurred vision, halos around lights and nausea. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Acute angle-closure glaucoma needs immediate treatment to lower eye pressure.

perOption.a: This is an emergency that can cause permanent vision loss.
perOption.c: This causes gradual central vision loss.
perOption.d: This causes redness and discharge without vision loss.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize acute angle-closure glaucoma.

questions.stem: The nurse teaches a client to use timolol eye drops. Which instruction reduces systemic side effects?

options.text: "Press on the inner corner of your eye for 1 to 2 minutes after the drop."

rationale.correct: Timolol is a beta-blocker; systemic absorption can cause bradycardia and bronchospasm.

perOption.a: This blocks drainage into the tear duct, reducing systemic absorption.
perOption.b: Blinking pumps the drug into the tear duct.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Reduce systemic absorption of eye drops.

questions.stem: A client reports sudden flashes of light, many new floaters and a feeling of a curtain coming down over one eye. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Arrange immediate evaluation for retinal detachment
Tell the client to rest and recheck in a week

rationale.correct: Retinal detachment is an emergency.

perOption.a: These are classic signs; prompt surgery can save vision.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize retinal detachment.

questions.stem: A client has age-related macular degeneration. Which tool should the nurse teach the client to use at home?

rationale.correct: Macular degeneration affects central vision; check daily with an Amsler grid.

perOption.a: The grid detects new distortion or blind spots in central vision.
perOption.b: This tests visual acuity in the clinic.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Which strategy is best when talking with an older adult who has hearing loss?

options.text: Face the client, speak clearly in a lower pitch and reduce background noise

rationale.correct: Presbycusis affects high frequencies; face the client, speak clearly and lower the pitch.

perOption.a: This makes lip-reading easier and improves hearing at the frequencies older adults keep.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Communicate with a client who has hearing loss.

questions.stem: A client with Ménière's disease is having an acute attack of vertigo. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Have the client lie still in a quiet, dim room

rationale.correct: Ménière's: vertigo, tinnitus and hearing loss; limit sodium and keep the client safe during attacks.

perOption.a: Movement and stimulation worsen the vertigo.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Manage an acute Ménière's attack.

questions.stem: For each disorder, indicate its characteristic finding.

columns.text: Ptosis that worsens later in the day

rationale.correct: Tell neurological disorders apart by their hallmark features.

perOption.r1:c2: Muscle fatigue worsens with use, so weakness increases later in the day.
perOption.r2:c1: Weakness begins in the legs and moves upward.
perOption.r4:c4: Heat slows conduction in demyelinated nerves.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
